business_problem: Computer Gross needed to give thousands of B2B ecommerce customers faster product discovery, quoting, and support because its 145,000-product catalog and growing customer base were overwhelming internal teams with repetitive questions and manual quote generation.
solution_summary: Computer Gross adopted IBM watsonx Assistant, built with watsonx.ai, as the conversational layer for a new self-service B2B commerce experience. IBM and partner teams mapped every customer interaction point and integrated the assistant into backend systems through GraphQL APIs so it could do more than answer FAQs. The assistant now understands natural-language product questions, searches a large catalog for the most relevant options, generates tailored quotes instantly based on customer conditions, and surfaces updates on orders, returns, and invoicing without waiting for human intervention. That combination turns the portal into an end-to-end guided buying and service environment rather than a static product catalog. Because customers can complete more of the purchasing journey independently, support and sales teams can focus on higher-value work while the business gains a scalable, round-the-clock customer engagement model suited to a very large reseller network.

data_flow: Customer questions flow through the watsonx Assistant interface, GraphQL APIs connect the assistant to product, pricing, and order systems, the platform returns relevant products or tailored quotes in real time, and resulting self-service actions reduce the need for manual support follow-up.
business_outcome: Computer Gross improved customer satisfaction, reduced response and ticket volume, raised quote conversion and order value, and lowered operating cost while creating a more autonomous B2B ecommerce journey.
